name: New York to Invisible Collar
summary: The move to Invisible Collar adds a high second-leg closure after arm isolation and neck clearing, reinforcing the bottom player's rubber-guard posture control.
description: New York to Invisible Collar keeps the trapped arm isolated, clears the head-side grip and closes the second leg high to reinforce the bottom player's clinch.
overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Clear the neck through the Chill Dog checkpoint before adding the second leg. Neither a jacket collar nor rear hooks define this route.

Keep the elbow separated from an inside frame before closing the second leg. Maintain the cleared hand position and knee hug as the free leg comes higher. Bring the second leg into the high clinch through hip motion; do not pull the foot into position against resistance.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): What must remain isolated during the leg change?
flashcards.answer: The overhook and knee hug keep one arm from returning inside while you add the reinforcing leg.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent's arm outside the inside-frame space

plausible: Their hand outside while the elbow wedges between your chests
Their wrist held against your chest with the elbow free
trap: Their upper arm covered but the forearm still across your chest

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): Which support must you retain when freeing the other leg?
flashcards.answer: Keep the raised knee supported over the isolated arm as the other leg begins to climb.
flashcards.answer_line: The knee hug around the already isolated arm

plausible: Only a grip on the back of the head
Only a loose ankle draped on the shoulder
trap: The wrist grip after releasing the knee from the arm

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): Where does the reinforcing leg close?
flashcards.answer: The second leg joins the high clinch behind the head rather than closing low around the waist or capturing a calf.

plausible: Low around the opponent's waist
Beside the upper arm with the foot left at the hip
trap: Across the upper back with the knee below the shoulder

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): How do you keep posture down without losing the arm trap?
flashcards.answer: The whole high-leg and arm configuration retains posture; avoid substituting a separate wrench on the neck.
flashcards.answer_line: Use the connected leg clinch and arm isolation

plausible: Let the arm escape and pull only the head
Drop both legs and keep a single wrist grip
trap: Hold the knees high with the arm wrap left open

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): What change warns that the arm trap is opening?
flashcards.answer: Track the elbow as the legs move; a recovered inside frame can undo the isolation even if the ankles remain high.
flashcards.answer_line: Their elbow reappears as an inside frame

plausible: Their isolated hand stays outside on the mat
Your supported knee stays close to your chest
trap: Their free elbow frames while the isolated elbow stays outside

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): If the high knee loses support, what is the fallback?
flashcards.answer: Recover ordinary guard with an inside knee and forearm when the supported high connection fails.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the clinch and restore inside frames

plausible: Keep the leg high using the ankle alone
Reach both hands after their escaping head
trap: Re-cross the high ankles with the unsupported knee still back

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): Why keep the raised knee supported as the other leg climbs?
flashcards.answer: Support the raised knee and move through a comfortable hip angle. Pulling the foot while the knee stays fixed substitutes twisting load for hip movement.
flashcards.answer_line: So hip movement supplies the angle without twisting the knee

plausible: To let the ankle pull replace any movement of the hip
To keep the hip flat while the foot is drawn higher
trap: So foot height alone can hold posture after the knee drifts

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): What must the head-side arm do before leg reinforcement?
flashcards.answer: Move through the Chill Dog neck-clearing checkpoint without abandoning New York arm isolation, then add the second high leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Clear around the head while the knee stays hugged

plausible: Return the opponent's hand to their chest
Release the overhook and reach both arms behind
trap: Stay in the original leg grip until both high legs close

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): What indicates a knee-loading error during entry?
flashcards.answer: Pulling the foot across a stationary knee applies twisting load. Move the hip to make space or reset the high leg.
flashcards.answer_line: The foot moves while the knee is held fixed

plausible: The hip turns with the supported knee
The second leg pauses before closing
trap: The hip makes space before the ankle changes position

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): What should the first closure drill preserve?
flashcards.answer: Rehearse adding the second high leg without losing the overhook and knee support, and stop before finishing pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm isolation while the second leg joins the clinch

plausible: Both elbows inside while the ankles go high
A low leg cross with the opponent upright
trap: An isolated wrist with the elbow still free to frame

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): What must open before changing a loaded hip angle?
flashcards.answer: Release the loaded connection before a large direction change so the shoulder and neck are not forced against the high legs.

plausible: Only the free foot while the upper loop stays taut
Only the ankle crossing while the overhook stays loaded
trap: Only the head-side grip while the high legs keep pulling

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (bottom): What distinguishes the destination from Chill Dog?
flashcards.answer: Chill Dog provides the neck-cleared arm trap; Invisible Collar adds the second high-leg reinforcement.
flashcards.answer_line: A second leg reinforcing the high head-side clinch

plausible: A higher first ankle with the free foot still low
A tighter knee hug around the same isolated arm
trap: The cleared hand regripping the original controlling leg

defender.description: New York to Invisible Collar (defender): The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure.
defender.overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Clear the neck through the Chill Dog checkpoint before adding the second leg. Neither a jacket collar nor rear hooks define this route.

The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure. Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.

Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm. Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens. Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Keep a balanced base: Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.
Address the leg enclosure: Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm.
Recover inside position: Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens.
Stop on compression: Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (top): Which movement should you prevent before it closes?
flashcards.answer: The extra high leg reinforces the existing clinch; early inside space can interrupt it before full closure.
flashcards.answer_line: The second leg joining behind your head

plausible: Their free foot returning to the floor
Their high knee lowering toward their ribs
trap: Their free knee returning inside below your shoulder

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (top): How should the trapped elbow relate to your torso?
flashcards.answer: Keeping the elbow near the ribs limits further arm separation while the high loop is being opened.
flashcards.answer_line: Stay compact rather than flaring away

plausible: Reach farther out across the mat
Hold it outside their knee while only the wrist returns
trap: Extend it forward while keeping your shoulder low

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (top): What is the useful response to increasing stack pressure?
flashcards.answer: If your pressure folds the partner onto the neck, reduce that load and seek slack rather than driving through.
flashcards.answer_line: Unload and recover space at the high leg

plausible: Increase forward force while widening the knees
Lift their hips higher while the legs stay locked
trap: Maintain forward weight until the second leg opens

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (top): What must be available before head withdrawal?
flashcards.answer: Head extraction needs an opened high-leg connection; moving the head while the shoulder remains fixed can load both.
flashcards.answer_line: Slack allowing the neck and shoulder to move together

plausible: A free hand but a tightly enclosed shoulder
An upright chest against a still-captured neck
trap: An open second leg with the original high thigh still tight

flashcards.question: New York to Invisible Collar (top): How do you avoid immediate re-isolation after release?
flashcards.answer: Use the opened connection to recover an inside frame rather than leaving the arm outside for another knee hug.
flashcards.answer_line: Bring the freed elbow back inside by the ribs

plausible: Leave the hand wide on the mat
Reach behind their back with the elbow flared
trap: Bring the hand in while leaving the elbow beyond their thigh
